shouldFix.title: G16-3 requires selectorDecision.ambiguity = refuse-only for C-MISSING-PLATFORM-METADATA, but the selector contains no platform rule of any kind, so the acceptance class demands an outcome the algorithm has no rule to produce
shouldFix.subjectEvidence: G16-3 now reads 'C-MISSING-OWNER, C-OWNER-OUTSIDE-UNIVERSE, C-MISSING-COMPONENT-DECLARATION, C-INCOMPLETE-UNIVERSE, C-PREDICATE-MISSING, and C-MISSING-PLATFORM-METADATA are REFUSE only (selectorDecision.ambiguity = refuse-only)'. That names a specific value of a specific selector output field for a specific change class. But the token 'platform' does not occur anywhere inside /selector - zero occurrences across authority, ownershipRecord, changeSet, algorithm, failSafe, mustNot and comparisonBasis. Step 3's REFUSE-only list has five conditions and none concerns platform metadata; ambiguityPolicy.law's list has four and none concerns it; comparisonBasis.law's has three. The only two clauses that state the consequence are G16-3 itself and /g16Tests/corpus/fixtureDomainBasis/missingMetadata, which says the case 'forces typed REFUSE/NON-PASS' - both inside the corpus and test node, neither inside the selector that emits the value.
shouldFix.counterexample: A harness builds the C-MISSING-PLATFORM-METADATA cell required by the corpus domain: a comparison-basis identity whose platform set is empty. Every changed unit resolves to exactly one in-universe owner, the component declaration is present, the universe is complete, and the predicate is present - so step 3 matches none of its five REFUSE-only conditions and none of its conflict conditions. The lawful emission is ambiguity = none. G16-3 requires refuse-only. The class fails on an implementation that followed the algorithm exactly, and the only way to pass is for the implementer to add a sixth classification condition the contract never states - which is precisely the invention of unstated selector authority that 'the ownership record is the only impact authority' exists to prevent.
shouldFix.impact: This does not create an under-selection escape: no lane is silently skipped, and fixtureDomainBasis still retains the cell. The defect is that the newest repair introduced a change class and an oracle entry for it without introducing the selector rule that makes the oracle satisfiable, so G16-3 is unimplementable as written for one of its six REFUSE-only classes. It is the enumeration-drift pattern that produced CLAUDE-V5-B1 and CLAUDE-V6-A2, appearing this time between the test node and the selector rather than within the selector.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Add the condition to step 3 and to ambiguityPolicy.law - a comparison-basis identity with a missing, empty, or invalid platform set is AMBIGUOUS-REFUSE-ONLY - so the classifier can emit what G16-3 requires. Alternatively, if the authors intend platform-metadata validity to be a corpus-domain property only and not a selector classification, then remove C-MISSING-PLATFORM-METADATA from G16-3's selectorDecision.ambiguity list and let fixtureDomainBasis.missingMetadata carry it alone as a NON-PASS obligation. Either resolution is one clause; the two must not disagree. /selector/algorithm and /g16Tests/classes are both already rostered paths.

shouldFix.title: fixtureDomainBasis.digestRule creates an evidence obligation with no acceptance class, so a harness that shrinks the domain and omits the pre-mutation digest passes every authored class
shouldFix.subjectEvidence: digestRule states 'A closed digest of the pre-mutation basis MUST appear on every corpus run. A harness that computes the domain after mutation is a failed successor.' That is an obligation on emitted evidence and it is the mechanism by which the MCICV6-B1 repair becomes checkable - without the pre-mutation digest there is nothing to compare a run's cell set against. The strings 'fixtureDomainBasis', 'nonShrinkLaw' and 'digestRule' occur nowhere in /g16Tests/classes. No class requires the domain digest to be emitted, and none requires the executed cell set to reconcile against it.
shouldFix.counterexample: A harness computes its domain after the hostile mutation, producing a strictly smaller cell set, emits results for every cell in that smaller set, and emits no pre-mutation domain digest. coverageLaw's requirement - 'Every cell in that exact domain MUST have a result' - is satisfied against the domain the harness computed, because nothing external fixes what the domain was. G16-1, G16-3, G16-9 and G16-10 all pass on the cells present. G16-13 checks the selectorDecisionDigest join, not the domain. Nothing fails. The behaviour is unlawful under digestRule and nonShrinkLaw, but it is undetectable from the emitted evidence, which is the property the blocker repair needed.
shouldFix.impact: MCICV6-B1 was a blocker about hostile domain shrink. v7's rules forbid it clearly, so this is not a licensed escape - but the repair's auditability depends on one emitted artifact that no class requires. This is the same shape as the finding this reviewer raised at v5 as CLAUDE-V5-S3, where the selectorDecisionDigest binding was stated in the selector output and no class enforced it; the process answered that one by creating G16-13. The identical treatment is owed to the newest emitted artifact.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Add a class - or extend G16-10 - requiring that every corpus run emit the closed pre-mutation fixtureDomainBasis digest, and that the executed cell set reconcile exactly against the basis that digest commits to, with any shortfall a failed successor. /g16Tests/classes is already on the roster.

systemicObservation: v7 is the strongest artifact in this chain and the second consecutive candidate with no blocker. Both surviving findings sit on the newest repair, and both are the same species the process already knows how to close. V7-S1 is enumeration drift - a new change class given an oracle entry without the matching rule in the clause that produces the value - which is CLAUDE-V5-B1 and CLAUDE-V6-A2 in a new location. V7-S2 is an emitted-evidence obligation with no acceptance class, which is CLAUDE-V5-S3 exactly, and the process answered that one by creating G16-13. The two mechanical checks this reviewer proposed at v5 would both have fired here at authoring time: when a repair adds a member to a set, grep every clause that enumerates that set - 'platform' returns zero hits inside /selector while G16-3 names a platform change class; and when a repair adds a required emitted artifact, grep the acceptance classes for its name - 'fixtureDomainBasis' returns zero hits inside /g16Tests/classes. Adding those two greps to the authoring pass, alongside the abolished-term grep, would have produced a zero-zero candidate this cycle. The substantive contract has now been stable for three generations: v7 changed no lane rule, no ownership rule and no evidence rule except to strengthen the ones the reviews named.
verdictBasis: Zero blockers and two SHOULD-FIX findings; the dispatch admits ACCEPT only at zero and zero. All six claimed repairs are real and verified against the subject's bytes, and because every frozen predecessor verdict was a permitted input this reviewer certified all five predecessor records directly - all exact. Both surviving findings were introduced by this cycle's MCICV6-B1 repair rather than carried, and neither creates an under-selection escape.
verdictStatement: v7 answers every finding from both v6 reviews, and answers two of them structurally rather than by another prose sweep: the live-pin locator is now a single standing field with every clause deferring to it, and the succession-metadata carve-out is defined as empty of re-measurement-block edits with a written standing rule. The corpus domain is now fixed before hostile mutation, roles are product-selected from DR-118 instead of read from the manifest, and hostile deletion cannot remove a cell - which closes a blocker this reviewer wrongly passed at v6 and has withdrawn above. Complete C-MULTI-OWNER is a MUST conflict-universe with REFUSE-only dominance stated in four places that agree. The roster is closed at zero off-roster paths, the PASS-NO-SCOPE-EFFECT claim is independently confirmed on the D-110 delta, and all five frozen predecessor verdicts are recorded exactly. What remains are two consequences of the newest repair. G16-3 requires selectorDecision.ambiguity = refuse-only for C-MISSING-PLATFORM-METADATA while the word platform appears nowhere in the entire selector, so the oracle demands a value the algorithm has no rule to emit. And fixtureDomainBasis.digestRule makes the pre-mutation domain digest the mechanism that renders the anti-shrink law auditable, while no acceptance class requires that digest to be emitted or reconciled - so a harness that computes its domain after mutation and omits the digest passes every authored class. Neither is an under-selection escape and neither is carried from an earlier cycle. DR-121 remains OPEN; DR-G16 remains PROPOSED, not QUALIFIED.
authorityOfThisVerdict: This verdict is a reviewer opinion recorded for coordinator disposition. It applies nothing, edits no subject, marks no row SATISFIED, marks no gate QUALIFIED, authorizes no implementation, chooses no CI vendor, mints no D-096 (A) grant, and does not touch docs/v2/architecture/08-decision-and-readiness-register.md or docs/coop/COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md. It also did not edit the review prompt it was given.
coordinatorNote: A v8 needs two rostered paths that are already rostered - /selector/algorithm and /g16Tests/classes - plus /selector/comparisonBasis for the advisory. No design work is outstanding: V7-S1 is a one-clause choice between adding the platform condition to step 3 or removing it from G16-3's selectorDecision list, and the coordinator should pick which, because the two answers differ on whether platform-metadata validity is a selector concern or a corpus-domain concern only. V7-S2 is one new class, or two sentences added to G16-10, mirroring what G16-13 did for the selectorDecisionDigest. Three process notes. First, this reviewer's v6 M-8 PASS on the dependent-product coverageLaw is withdrawn in this verdict; Codex's MCICV6-B1 was correct and the v6 verdict should not be read as independent corroboration of that formulation. Second, keeping frozen predecessor verdicts readable while barring the concurrent reviewer has now paid off in three consecutive cycles and is what let this verdict certify all five predecessor records; it is worth stating explicitly in future prompts. Third, the two authoring-time greps named in the systemic observation would have caught both surviving findings before dispatch.
